transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um... is it okay if I just jump right in? 

Okay, great. Well, I guess I'm here because... gosh, I hope this doesn't make me sound like a difficult person to work with, because I really do pride myself on being professional and getting along with everyone. But... for almost two years now, ever since this one commission I did, I've just been unable to shake this certainty that a few people in my ensemble are... well, quietly undermining my work. 

I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, I'm sorry. It's just... they use these little things to do it. Like sudden schedule changes, or weird seating choices, or just these tiny little comments during rehearsals. And they'll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain why it all happened, and I always nod and try to be polite about it, but... I just can't shake the fact that it's intentional. 

I don't know, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm handling the situation the right way, if that's alright.
When you’re shown those emails or notes that explain what happened, do you still believe the people are intentionally undermining you?

Um... yes. I mean, I really try to be objective about it, I promise I do. I don't want to be the kind of director who ignores evidence or, you know, causes a fuss. But... yeah, even when they show me those emails or the notes that supposedly explain it all away... I just still have this deep-down certainty that it's intentional. 

I look at the emails, and I smile and say 'thank you for clarifying,' because I really want to keep the peace and be easy to work with. But... I just can't shake the fact that they are quietly undermining my work. It's been almost two years since that commission, and that certainty just hasn't changed, no matter what they show me. 

Is it terrible that I still feel that way? I know it probably sounds a bit stubborn. I just hope I don't sound completely unreasonable to you... does that make sense?
Have you ever been able to completely reconsider this belief and decide that maybe they are not undermining you?

Um... I really wish I could say yes to that. I know a good director is supposed to be flexible and, you know, take things at face value. And I promise you, I have tried so hard to just let it go. I'll sit there and tell myself that maybe I'm just overthinking it, and that the sudden schedule changes or the seating choices and the little comments in rehearsals don't actually mean anything. 

But... I just can't. For almost two years now, ever since that commission, I've just been completely unable to shake the certainty that they are quietly undermining my work. Even when I look right at the emails they show me to explain it all, that certainty just... it just stays there. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound completely irrational or impossible to work with. I really do try to be reasonable and open-minded about it all. Am I making sense?
Have you felt this way about people frequently, across different situations, since early adulthood?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm, you know, a suspicious person or someone who's generally hard to get along with. Because I'm really not, I promise. 

Throughout grad school and... well, just in my life generally, I've always prided myself on being a team player. I usually have really wonderful relationships with the musicians and producers I work with. It's really just... just this one specific situation, with this particular ensemble, ever since that commission two years ago. 

Before that, I never really had any issues like this with anyone. I've always tried to see the best in people, and I really value collaboration above almost anything else. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure you know I'm usually very easygoing and open with people.
Have you ever found concrete evidence that these people were actually trying to undermine you?

Um... well, no. I mean, not what you would probably call concrete evidence. I really don't want to sound like I'm making baseless accusations, because I know how that looks. I've never caught them, you know, saying it on a recording or found a secret memo that spells it out. 

I just... I see the little things, the things that are so hard to prove to anyone else. Like the way a piece is programmed in a concert, or the tone someone uses when they ask a question during rehearsal. It's those subtle things that just add up in my mind. But as far as hard, undeniable proof that I could show you or a board of directors... no, I haven't found anything like that. 

I know that probably makes it sound like it's all in my head, and I really, really try to consider that possibility. I don't want to be someone who just imagines the worst in people. Does that sound okay? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough.
Do you feel this kind of suspicion toward other people in your life as well, or is it only about this one ensemble?

Um, no, it's really just them. I promise, I'm not walking around looking over my shoulder or suspecting everyone I meet. I really want to be clear about that, because I know how it can sound when I talk about this ensemble. 

But honestly, outside of this one specific issue, my life is... well, it's really quite normal and productive. I'm still meeting all my deadlines for my other projects, and I'm keeping up with my composing just fine. I even still go for my runs most mornings, which helps clear my head. And things at home with my wife are... they're really good, basically steady and happy. 

I just try to focus on all those positive things and keep the situation with the ensemble from affecting the rest of my life. I really hope that shows that I'm still functioning well and keeping things in perspective. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure you see that this isn't taking over my whole life.
Have you ever had any beliefs like this about people trying to undermine you before this two-year period?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... I really want to be clear about that, because I'd hate for you to think I've just always been, you know, a suspicious person or someone who holds grudges. Before this... this whole situation, I never had any thoughts like that at all. 

It really just started... well, it's been about a year and nine months ago now. Right after I won that commission I mentioned, and they actually invited me to conduct the premiere. That's when things sort of... shifted with them. But before that exact point in time, absolutely nothing like this had ever crossed my mind. 

I hope that answers your question? I'm trying to be as exact as I can with the timeline for you, so please let me know if you need me to clarify anything else. I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Since this started, has it caused you to have problems keeping up with work or your daily responsibilities?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely haven't lost any work over it, and I'm still taking care of myself just fine, like I said about my runs and my other composing projects. I really try hard not to let it affect my actual output. 

I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, the main thing is just that rehearsals and, you know, professional emails with them take a bit more energy now. I find myself rereading their decisions a few times, or maybe asking for extra clarification on things, just to be absolutely sure we're on the same page. But it hasn't stopped me from doing my job or keeping up with my daily life. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult to work with. I just like to be thorough. Does that sound like a reasonable way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm managing things the right way.
